name: Ribbon Gamma Oracle unrestricted setAssetPricer
summary: Oracle.setAssetPricer in Ribbon's Gamma fork is declared external with no owner restriction and only guards the replacement case, so any caller can install an arbitrary pricer contract for an asset that has no pricer yet. The attacker registered pricers he controlled for stETH, AAVE, LINK and PAXG, used the equally unrestricted Whitelist.whitelistCollateral and whitelistProduct to create four oToken series against them, then pushed expiry prices inflated by 1e10 and redeemed a dust position for almost the entire collateral held in the shared MarginPool.
notes: Non-upgradeable Ribbon Gamma Oracle. Its runtime code hash is 0xf5051947510487306a66d6adc9095b992fc8ea4e76e5d6846870888af2f77bc8 at the deployment block 14416610, at block 23954876 immediately before the anchor, and at block 23995263 immediately before the first redeem; the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero and the contract holds no delegatecall path, so the executed code never changed after deployment.

Components are the net token movement of the Gamma MarginPool 0x3c212a044760de5a529b3ba59363ddeccc2210be across the eight campaign transactions in source-5: the pool receives 0.068 WETH, 0.083 wstETH, 100 USDC and 0.0028 WBTC of attacker collateral when the four oToken series are minted in 0x9b686c9d95, and pays out 323.748462037559855726 WETH, 371.753847784297541009 wstETH, 192,612.423528 USDC and 2.75850126 WBTC across the six redeem transactions; the attacker inputs are netted out. The assets left the pool on 2025-12-12, six days after the anchor, which loss.realizedAt records and which the valuation timestamps use; at the anchor timestamp the same quantities would be USD 2,808,028.08. Published figures of USD 2.3-2.7 million are Aevo's vault-level accounting after the announced 19 percent withdrawal haircut and are not netted out here. DefiLlama observations lie within 31 seconds of the valuation timestamp; USDC uses par, 0.03 percent above the DefiLlama observation.

Re-anchored from 0xb73e45948f4aabd77ca888710d3685dd01f1c81d24361d4ea0e4b4899d490e1e. That transaction is the price-poisoning step and executes only attacker-deployed machinery plus correctly behaving victim code; the defect executed for the first time six days earlier in the permissionless Oracle.setAssetPricer call used as the new anchor.
